# cuteafd-eval

> Measurements of CuteAFD and tpurtell's vLLM fork serving quantized GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoints on one machine
> (2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, 300 W). Results-first; nothing here is a recommendation. Maintained by Michael M
> (UrbanAstroLA).

## Read these first
- https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/findings.json: every finding (one measured quantity: statement, class, status, sign, unit, n, interval,
  scope, family, replication, evidence pointers into results/) and every judgement (strength, basis, does_not_show).
- https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/runs.json: every run, its goals (sub-questions, design, status) and the files each goal owns.
- https://github.com/UrbanAstroLA/cuteafd-eval/tree/main/results: the frozen data, one folder per run.

## How to read a finding
- class: difference (interval excludes 0) | not detected (interval includes 0; `bound` gives the largest effect not
  excluded) | descriptive (counts, no interval) | source reading | accounting.
- status: protocol | amendment | follow-up (declared before its own data) | post hoc | exploratory | check.
- family: how many intervals were computed alongside it and how many excluded 0. Intervals are not corrected for
  multiplicity unless a protocol said so.
- Do not read 'not detected' as 'no difference'. Do not generalise past `scope` (one model, one machine).
- Fixtures are not comparable across model families; KL and NLL are per tokenizer.

## Current judgements (strength: established > supported > indicated > open)
- Where does most of a configuration's distance from the BF16 model come from: the routed experts, the core, or the engine? Mostly from the routed experts: 3.25-bit to 4-bit experts moved teacher-panel KL by −0.0195; the engine moved it by +0.0035 at most and the core by less. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/precision.html#s-S-experts
- On the same weights, is CuteAFD farther from the BF16 model than the vLLM fork? Slightly: +0.0017 (K3.25) and +0.0035 (K4) on the teacher panel, +0.0054 and +0.0090 on long code; not detected below 8K or in NLL at 32K-128K. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/precision.html#s-S-engine-gap
- How much of CuteAFD's long-code gap do its FP8 settings account for? On K3.25 most of the long-code gap goes with W8A16 prefill; on K4 no setting tried closes it (best: W8A16 + amax, −0.0061 of +0.0090). [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/precision.html#s-S-fp8-settings
- Does distance from BF16, measured to 14.4K, predict accuracy at long context? Only in part: K3.25-Core-FP8 is farthest and scored lowest at 127K, but compact sits with hqa and anchor on distance and scored below hqa at 127K. [indicated] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/precision.html#s-S-distance-tasks
- Can distances from BF16 be compared across studies and CuteAFD releases? Yes on CuteAFD: the same weights give the same rows across v3.0.1, v4.0.0 and v5.0.0 (K3.25-Core-FP8 0.0476 on all three). [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/precision.html#s-S-reproducible
- Does accuracy on long-context tasks fall with length, and does core precision cause the fall? Yes, in every configuration including the BF16 core (anchor 0.985 at 4K to 0.918 at 127K); much of it is replies that did not finish. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/long-tasks.html#s-S-long-fall
- Where does a configuration's precision show up as a cost on long-context tasks? K3.25-Core-FP8 scored 0.051-0.058 below three 4-bit-expert configurations at 127K; nothing was detected at 4K and 16K. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/long-tasks.html#s-S-long-cost
- Does the compact attention mode cost accuracy at long context? Against hqa at 127K, yes (+0.037); against the BF16 core, not detected. [indicated] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/long-tasks.html#s-S-long-cost-compact
- Do long replies (to 130K tokens) finish and pass their checks on both engines? Yes for code and math on both engines (7-8 of 8 at the 130K cap); JSON validity varies; CuteAFD's replies are shorter. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/long-tasks.html#s-S-long-output
- Do the engines accept and use prompts of 256K to 1M tokens? In a one-request pilot, yes: both engines found the needle at 256K-1M tokens. [indicated] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/long-tasks.html#s-S-long-retrieval
- Does the core's precision change when the model decides to stop thinking on science questions? Not detected on either engine (11 + 30 questions on the vLLM fork, 41 on CuteAFD); shifts beyond about 0.05 in log p are excluded. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/thinking.html#s-S-think-stop
- Does the core's precision change how long the model thinks in free generation on science questions? Not known: one question on one engine, inconclusive (0.80 [0.51, 1.14]). [open] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/thinking.html#s-S-think-science-length
- Why does CuteAFD's BF16-core arm think shorter on code than its native 6-bit-core arm? Mostly CuteAFD's FP8 KDA setting: switching it off lengthened code thinking 1.31x, about the whole gap; on the vLLM fork the two cores think alike (1.00 [0.96, 1.04]). [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/thinking.html#s-S-think-code-kda
- Does shorter thinking cost correctness on code? Not settled: the 1.26x length gap came with no detected pass-rate difference (+1.6 points [−7.8, +10.9]), but an all-BF16-path arm passed more often in a post hoc look. [open] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/thinking.html#s-S-think-correctness
- What does CuteAFD v5's default attention mode (hqa) trade against a BF16 core? 4,266 MiB less than the BF16 core, with no task cost detected (+0.003 [−0.005, +0.012]). [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/settings.html#s-S-set-attention
- What does the compact attention mode trade against hqa? 2,568 MiB less than hqa, and below hqa at 127K (+0.037). [indicated] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/settings.html#s-S-set-compact
- What does turning CuteAFD's FP8 settings off cost in speed and memory? W8A16 prefill: about 4% first-token time; BF16 KDA and head: a smaller KV pool (1,931,264 to 1,215,488 tokens on K4-Core-K6), and BF16 KDA did not fit a K4 serving launch on v3.0.1. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/settings.html#s-S-set-costs
- Between the two 4-bit checkpoints, K4 and K4-Core-K6, is either closer to the BF16 model? Neither on both sets: level on the teacher panel (which can favour K4), K4-Core-K6 closer on the fidelity set (−0.0049). [open] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/checkpoints.html#s-S-ckpt-k6-k4
- How does the EXLR8 K4 checkpoint compare with the K4-Core-K6 configurations? Not detected to differ on tasks over four passes; farther from BF16 on the fidelity set, level on the teacher panel. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/checkpoints.html#s-S-ckpt-exlr8
- Is CuteAFD faster than the vLLM fork on this machine? On v4.0.0, faster or level in every measured cell on K3.25 and K4 (0 slower); v3.0.1 was slower at 1K with 8 streams and in first token with many streams. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/speed.html#s-S-speed-engines
- Does K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core cost speed on CuteAFD? Slower than K4 by 5-15% (v4 run); per-cell bands for this contrast were not published. [indicated] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/speed.html#s-S-speed-k6
- How much context fits, and how long does a start take? CuteAFD v4.0.0: larger KV pools (1,931,264 vs 1,377,179 tokens on K4) and ready in 81-91 s against 257-349 s. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/running.html#s-S-run-capacity
- Does the same request give the same result twice? CuteAFD: bit-identical across launches, days and releases. vLLM fork: varies beyond its first prefill chunk. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/running.html#s-S-run-determinism
- Do the engines reuse a repeated prompt? CuteAFD: yes (0.017 s for a repeated 8K prompt). vLLM fork: only in whole 4,352-token blocks, nothing below 17,408 tokens. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/running.html#s-S-run-prefix
- Does multi-turn tool calling differ between the engines or checkpoints? All arms 158-163 of 176; the engines differ on 5-7 of 88 scenarios; CuteAFD repeats exactly. [supported] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/tools.html#s-S-tools
- Do leads found after looking at the data hold on new data? Not in these runs: five leads found after looking each shrank or failed on new data or more passes. [established] https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/preview/method.html#s-M-leads

## Runs
- 2026-10-26 2026-10-26-cuteafd-setup-checks: Are the Core-FP8 checkpoint's bytes what its provenance says relative to K3.25-v1, and does CuteAFD v3.0.1 share, in source, the vLLM-engine issues D1-D7 and E1 found in earlier evaluation?
- 2026-10-26 2026-10-26-cuteafd-vs-vllm: How do tpurtell's CuteAFD v3.0.1 and his vLLM fork v0.9.2, each as shipped on GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 K3.25 with identical expert bytes on 2 RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q, compare in teacher-anchored precision, serving throughput and long-output behaviour under a frozen protocol?
- 2026-10-26 2026-10-26-e1-router-route: Are CuteAFD's GLM-5.3-Flash router logits bit-identical across the switch between its skinny GEMV route (up to 160 rows) and its TMA tensor-core route, a question its source audit left open?
- 2026-10-27 2026-10-27-k4-vllm-cuteafd: With brandonmusic's K4 checkpoint, how do tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 and CuteAFD v3.0.1 compare in distance from BF16, throughput and long-output behaviour under a protocol frozen before the first comparison request, and which CuteAFD settings move its precision difference?
- 2026-10-27 2026-10-27-long-context-pilot: Do tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 and CuteAFD v3.0.1, serving K3.25, accept prompts of 256K, 512K and 1M tokens and return planted needles from them?
- 2026-10-27 2026-10-27-vllm-startup-cache: How much does persisting the TileLang, Triton, TorchInductor and CUDA JIT caches shorten the startup of tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on this setup?
- 2026-10-30 2026-10-30-cuteafd-v4: Does CuteAFD v4.0.0 change precision, speed, memory and long-output behaviour against v3.0.1 and against tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, and how far is each checkpoint, including K4-Core-K6, from BF16?
- 2026-11-02 2026-11-02-thinking-length: Does storing K4-Core-K6's 316 core tensors in 6 bits instead of BF16 make the model think longer, on the vLLM fork with a local loader modification?
- 2026-11-02 2026-11-02-tool-calling: Does multi-turn tool calling work, and does its tool-eval-bench outcome differ, between CuteAFD v4.0.0 and tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 (same K4 checkpoint; on K3.25 each engine runs its own variant, Core-FP8 on CuteAFD and v1 on the vLLM fork)?
- 2026-11-03 2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, is K4-Core-K6's longer thinking against K4 associated with its 6-bit core or with its routed experts?
- 2026-11-05 2026-11-05-attn-position: On the 93 fixed science-question traces, does the core's effect on next-token distributions or on the stop decision build up with position, and do q_b and the output projections in BF16 together move the stop decision?
- 2026-11-05 2026-11-05-code-thinking: On code tasks on CuteAFD v4.0.0, does K4-Core-K6 with its native 6-bit core think longer than the same checkpoint with its BF16 core converted to FP8 at load?
- 2026-11-06 2026-11-06-cuteafd-fp8-ablation: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, which of the FP8 settings applied to the BF16-core checkpoint (KDA projections, vocabulary head, prefill activations) goes with its shorter code reasoning against the native 6-bit core?
- 2026-11-06 2026-11-06-new-questions: Does the q_b + output-projection stop-decision shift found on 11 science-question questions, and the core's (absent) effect on the stop decision, hold on 30 new questions on both engines?
- 2026-11-06 2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking: On the vLLM fork with the route-b loader, where only the core's weight values differ between arms, does K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core change code thinking length against the original BF16 core, and does the result agree with CuteAFD's?
- 2026-11-10 2026-11-10-context-probe: On CuteAFD v5.0.0 with two RTX PRO 6000, what does the precision of the tensors outside the K4 experts (BF16 core, BF16 q_b_proj and o_proj with K6 elsewhere, K6 core) buy on graded tasks as context grows from 4K to 127K tokens, delivered as one message and over eight turns?
